units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 11:2">Kel. XI, 2</cite>; <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 12">Num. R. s. 12</cite>, v. <cite ref="Q00412"><he>פּוֹתָה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Eruvin 10:12">Erub. X, 12</cite> <he>מחזירין צ׳ התחתון</he> you may bring back to its socket the lower pivot (of a door of a chest &c.).
<cite ref="Yoma 39b:12">Yoma 39ᵇ</cite> <he>וצ׳ דלתות וכ׳</he> the turning hinges of the Temple door were heard &c.; a. fr.—Pl. <he>צִירִים</he>, <he>צִירִין</he>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Nazir 8:1:10">Y. Naz. VIII, 57ᵃ</cite> bot <he>איסטרטיוטות שומרי צ׳ וכ׳</he> (not <he>ושומרי</he>) Roman soldiers were stationed in Jerusalem as guards of the hinges (of the Temple gates); <cite ref="Tosefta Pesachim 7:13">Tosef. Pes. VII, 13</cite> <he>צורים</he> ed. Zuck. (corr. acc.).

<cite ref="Bekhorot 45a:18">Bekh. 45ᵃ</cite> <he>כשם שצ׳ לבית כך צ׳ לאשה</he> as a house has hinges (doors moving in sockets), so a woman’s body has hinges (in her sexual organs; ref. to <cite ref="I Samuel 4:19">I Sam. IV, 19</cite> <he>צִרֶיהָ</he>).
<cite ref="I Samuel 4:19">Ib.</cite> <he>צִירֵי בשר</he> (the sockets and pivots in the male body are merely) hinges of flesh (muscles, not separate organs); a. e.
